lots.what_it_is: Bentwood side chair in the Thonet No. 14 pattern with a recent-looking cane seat. Catalogued as Josef Hofmann, Austrian, but no maker mark is visible and the paper tag is unreadable even enlarged.

lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep and flip maximums are 0. Score of 4 reflects a common No. 14 pattern chair: unmarked or copy examples usually trade around $30-80, a stamped period Thonet or Kohn could be more, but that is unproven here.

lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Double hoop back, ring stretcher, four splayed legs, classic No. 14 form. Cane seat looks bright and evenly coloured, likely a replacement. Paper lot tag enlarged with Pillow: writing illegible. No visible stamp, paper label or branding. The Hoffmann attribution does not fit this model, which is the generic Thonet No. 14 pattern.
lots.condition: Frame appears sound in the photo with honey-brown finish and some wear; seat likely re-caned. Underside not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a maker stamp, paper label or branded mark under the seat rail or inside the ring (Thonet, J&J Kohn, Fischel, Mundus)? What is the basis for the Josef Hofmann attribution, and is the cane seat original or replaced?

Bulk secondhand art books usually sell as a lot well below the sum of single-copy asking prices; a likely value of roughly $30-80 for three boxes gives score 3. A $4.00 secondhand shop sticker on one Cossington Smith title supports the low value.

lots.dropped_entries: All dropped. (3) Sydney Rare Book Auctions via Invaluable, box of gallery catalogues, estimate AUD 100-200, 2021-02-13: unverified, result unknown, over 24 months old, different content. (4) Elizabeth's Bookshop, Creating Australia, AUD 18: unverified single-title asking price. (5) ebay.de 236191992519, Cossington Smith A Life from Drawings, AUD 36.55: unverified, and not confirmed as the title in the lot. (6) ebay.de 204047793649, Cossington Smith by Daniel Thomas, AUD 60: unverified single-copy asking. (7) Room and Book, St Ives 1939-64, GBP 28: unverified, described as a new-book list price, edition may differ, GBP rate was a rough guess.
